content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I’m facing an issue where a [product_name] system keeps stopping. The setup includes a [product_name] with two [product_name] modules and an [product_name] analog module. To expand the I/O, another [product_name] with a [product_name] module is connected as a networked slave, along with a [product_name] operator device. Networking is handled via a [product_name] hub. The installation dates back to 2016 and was programmed using [product_name] V8. There were no initial issues. Toward the end of last year, I updated the program to add two weekly timer function blocks in [product_name] V8.1. After that, the system began stopping frequently, disrupting production. Even after removing the changes in [product_name] V8.1, the problem persisted. I then completely rewrote the program using V8.1, but it made things worse. Reverting to the original V8.0 program hasn't resolved the issue. What might cause the system to keep stopping? I’ve used timer blocks in other setups without networking issues. I’ve attached the program for review. Thank you for any help.

Which [article_no] are you using? Is it the standard [article_no] with firmware V1.08.03 (FS03)? This specific [product_name] often has issues—goes to stop irregularly—if it has a display and is networked. The trouble only happens during networking. If this matches your situation, unfortunately, it’s a known, unreparable error. If your device is still under warranty, consider submitting a claim.

Hello [user_name], Appreciate your response. I believe that's the firmware version we have. I heard there was an announcement from [company_name] in October 2016, and since we purchased our units in spring 2016, they probably are the FS03 batch. Thanks for your help.

This issue has been recognized since August 2016. However, [company_name] delayed the official notification until the updated [product_name] with FS:04 became available for shipment. Product updates: [product_name] (FS:04)

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that their [product_name] with display is unexpectedly stopping, particularly when networked and after program modifications using [product_name] V8.1. Even reverting to previous software versions and removing recent changes doesn’t resolve the issue. The root cause appears to be a firmware issue related to a specific [article_no] standard version with display, known to be unrepairable. This fault is causing interruption to production.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to provide dependable performance, regardless of software changes or networking status, and not experience random stoppages or impact production processes.
